narrative.intro: Harris obligated $1.2B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Harris won 11 awards this fiscal year, with an average award size of $107M and obligations up 27.7% year over year. Harris climbed from $376M in FY21 to $313M in FY22, $386M in FY23, $459M in FY24, $918M in FY25, and $1.2B in FY26. Harris shows a multi-year increase in reported obligations, with the FY25 to FY26 figure more than doubling some earlier single-year totals. Harris’s current-year totals are partial, and the award-value figures in some tables represent total contract values rather than only obligations. Harris’s mix of relatively large average award size and a modest award count suggests fewer, larger awards are driving the FY2026 to date totals. Harris’s year-over-year change and the fiscal-year sequence provide a clear numeric picture of recent federal contracting activity for procurement planners, competitors, and program managers tracking prime obligations and award sizing.

sections.heading: How large are Harris’s FY2026 federal obligations and how did they change year over year?
sections.body: Harris obligated $1.2B in FY2026 to date. Harris’s obligations are up 27.7% year over year, with an average award size of $107M across 11 awards. Harris’s fiscal-year history shows $376M in FY21, $313M in FY22, $386M in FY23, $459M in FY24, and $918M in FY25, leading into the current $1.2B figure.

sections.heading: Does Harris’s award count and award size indicate concentration in its federal portfolio?
sections.body: Harris has 11 awards in FY2026 to date with an average award size of $107M. Harris’s combination of a single-digit award count and a six-figure average award size points to concentration in larger awards rather than many small awards. Harris’s multi-year obligations also show growth in total dollars allocated to a smaller number of sizable contracts.
